message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, grouped by region:

| Region | Airport (IATA) | City | State | Notes |
|--------|----------------|------|-------|-------|
| **East Coast** | JFK | New York | NY | Major international hub, 6 runways |
| | BOS | Boston | MA | Hub for Northeast flights |
| | IAD | Washington, D.C. | VA | Primary airport for the DC area |
| | ATL | Atlanta | GA | One of the busiest airports worldwide |
| | CLT | Charlotte | NC | Major hub for American Airlines |
| **Midwest** | ORD | Chicago | IL | Second busiest airport in the U.S. |
| | DEN | Denver | CO | Hub for Southwest and United |
| | MSP | Minneapolis | MN | Major hub for Delta |
| | DTW | Detroit | MI | Hub for Delta |
| **South** | MCO | Orlando | FL | Major hub for domestic and international flights |
| | PHX | Phoenix | AZ | Hub for Southwest |
| | LAX | Los Angeles | CA | Major international hub |
| | LAS | Las Vegas | NV | Hub for Southwest |
| **West Coast** | SFO | San Francisco | CA | Major hub for United |
| | SEA | Seattle | WA | Hub for Alaska Airlines |
| | SAN | San Diego | CA | Hub for Southwest |
| | HOU | Houston | TX | Major hub for United |
| **Alaska & Hawaii** | ANC | Anchorage | AK | Major hub for Alaska Airlines |
| | HNL | Honolulu | HI | Major hub for Hawaiian Airlines |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger traffic, flight operations, and connectivity. They serve as major hubs for both domestic and international travel.
